\section*{Problem Set 2: Kinematics}

\subsection*{Problem 1}

A cart starts from rest and speeds up at a steady rate. Its average velocity over a
time interval is
\begin{equation}
  \bar{v} = \frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} = \frac{x_f - x_0}{t_f - t_0}.
  \label{eq:average}
\end{equation}
\begin{enumerate}
  \renewcommand{\labelenumi}{(\alph{enumi})}
  \item Find the average velocity between $t = 0$ and $t = 4.0\ \mathrm{s}$.
  \item Explain why the instantaneous velocity at $t = 2.0\ \mathrm{s}$ equals it.
  \item Sketch the position of the cart against time.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Problem 2}

Starting from the definition of acceleration, the speed after a distance $d$ follows
from three steps:
\begin{align*}
  v^2 &= v_0^2 + 2 a d \\
      &= 0 + 2 \left(3.0\ \mathrm{m/s^2}\right)\left(12\ \mathrm{m}\right) \\
      &= 72\ \mathrm{m^2/s^2}.
\end{align*}
Which value is closest to the final speed?
\begin{enumerate}
  \renewcommand{\labelenumi}{\Alph{enumi}.}
  \item $6.0\ \mathrm{m/s}$
  \item $8.5\ \mathrm{m/s}$
  \item $36\ \mathrm{m/s}$
  \item $72\ \mathrm{m/s}$
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Problem 3}

A stone falls from rest. Ignoring air resistance, the distance it falls in time $t$ is
\begin{equation}
  d = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 ,
  \label{eq:fall}
\end{equation}
and the time to fall a height $h$ is
\begin{equation}
  t = \sqrt{\frac{2 h}{g}} .
  \label{eq:time}
\end{equation}
Use $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ in both parts:
\begin{enumerate}
  \renewcommand{\labelenumi}{(\roman{enumi})}
  \item how far does it fall in $1.5\ \mathrm{s}$?
  \item how long does it take to fall $20\ \mathrm{m}$?
\end{enumerate}
2.5 metres is the height of the classroom ceiling, for comparison.
